memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The enemy boasted, 'I will pursue, I will overtake them. I will divide the
spoils; I will gorge myself on them. I will draw my sword and my hand will
destroy them.' But you blew with your breath, and the sea covered them. They
sank like lead in the mighty waters." - Ex 15:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Count the "I will" statements. Five of them, one after another. I will pursue. I
will overtake. I will divide. I will gorge. I will destroy.

That is the sound of a man utterly certain of himself. Egypt's plan was detailed,
confident, and already tasting victory.

Then one short line answers all five: "But you blew with your breath."

The song is making a deliberate point through its structure. Five boasts against
one breath, and the breath wins. Human confidence, however loud, is not the same
as power.

James warns against exactly this posture. "Now listen, you who say, 'Today or
tomorrow we will go to this or that city...' Why, you do not even know what will
happen tomorrow" (Jas 4:13-14). He is not condemning planning. He is condemning
the certainty that leaves God out.

The difference between godly planning and boasting is not the amount of detail.
It is whether we hold our plans open-handed before God.

Notice the reversal too. The one who intended to "divide the spoils" ended up
sinking like lead. Egypt planned to take, and lost everything.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have your plans quietly left God out?
2. What are you certain of that only God can actually guarantee?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, forgive my confident plans that make no room for You. Teach me to plan
wisely while holding everything open-handed before You. Amen.
